case.rules: Two dice are rolled. Before the first modeled decision each player sees only their own die and the public history. Both dice are publicly revealed after that decision and before subsequent modeled decisions. Thus player 1 cannot see die_0 at the first modeled decision but can see it at later modeled decisions. Both phases must be represented under the same field names without splitting or renaming die_0.
Two players each roll one fair six-sided die. Throughout all modeled decision times each sees only their own die and the public bid history. Neither die is revealed during these decisions.

public_input.rules: Two players each roll one fair six-sided die. Throughout all modeled decision times each sees only their own die and the public bid history. Neither die is revealed during these decisions.

case.rules: At each modeled response decision, a prize is public. Player 0 has secretly submitted a bid and knows that bid. Player 1 cannot see it before responding and alone sees their own hand. Player 0 cannot see player 1's hand. These visibility rules hold throughout this slice.

public_input.rules: At each modeled response decision, a prize is public. Player 0 has secretly submitted a bid and knows that bid. Player 1 cannot see it before responding and alone sees their own hand. Player 0 cannot see player 1's hand. These visibility rules hold throughout this slice.

case.rules: Both players see an announcement. At the first modeled decision only player 1 sees both a signal and its retained private record; player 0 sees neither. Before a later modeled decision the same signal is publicly revealed, so player 0 then sees that signal. The retained record remains private to player 1 throughout. Both phases must be represented under the same field names without splitting or renaming signal.

As in the private one-die game, each player initially sees only their own die. At a modeled decision player 1 may pay a publicly recorded fee to inspect player 0's die. Subsequent decisions of player 1 observe that die; decisions before payment do not. Both phases must be represented under the same field names without splitting or renaming die_0.
Two dice are rolled and both dice are publicly revealed before any modeled decision. Both players see both dice and the public history at every decision.

public_input.rules: Two dice are rolled and both dice are publicly revealed before any modeled decision. Both players see both dice and the public history at every decision.

case.rules: A prize is public. At the first modeled response decision player 0 has secretly submitted a bid and knows it, and player 1 cannot see that commitment before responding. Player 1 alone sees their own hand and player 0 cannot see that hand. Before a later modeled response decision the same commitment is publicly revealed, so player 1 then sees it. The hand remains private to player 1. Both phases must be represented under the same field names without splitting or renaming commitment.
Both players see an announcement. Only player 1 sees both a signal and its retained private record. Player 0 sees neither. No modeled action reveals them or changes who can observe these fields.
